content.text: The text recounts General Gordon’s heroic defense of Khartoum: he fortified the city, organized troops and supplies, sent refugees and steamers away, but weakened his position while awaiting a tardy British expedition. Government indecision and Lord Wolseley’s slow, oversized relief operation failed; Khartoum fell on 26 January 1885, and Gordon was killed. It then presents romances and legends involving Cota’s pinto horse, Edward Bray’s rescue of Eugenia on a mountain trail, and their eventual partnership; and Miss Trotter’s discovery that Chris Calton loved her, followed by their marriage. Finally, it narrates Louis XVI’s imprisonment in the Temple, trial, execution at the Place de la Révolution, Marie Antoinette’s execution at the Conciergerie, Madame Elisabeth’s death, the Dauphin’s confinement and death in the Temple, and Madame Royale’s release, journey to Vienna, marriage at Mittau, and later exile and return to France.
